name: @projexlight/sdk-webhook
summary: Outbound webhook delivery for ProjexCloud: register Endpoints, subscribe them to event types, publish events through the queue, and a worker retries with exponential backoff + signed HMAC. Failed deliveries land in the per-tenant DLQ for replay from the tenant-admin Webhooks page. Subscription keys are vault-stored signing references — never raw secrets.

endpoints.description: Register a new endpoint (URL + signing-key vault ref + tenant_id).
Subscribe an endpoint to one or more event type names (e.g. 'tenant.created.v1').
Publish an event to every subscribed endpoint. Usually internal — other SDKs call into emitEvent and we pick it up.
List delivery rows (filterable by tenant, endpoint, status). The DLQ view in tenant-admin reads this.
Force-replay a DLQ delivery; restarts attempt count from 1.

events.name: webhook.endpoint.registered.v1
events.description: New endpoint persisted; carries the signing key vault ref (not the secret itself).

events.name: webhook.delivery.attempted.v1
events.description: One delivery attempt completed (success or failure); carries http_status + duration_ms.

events.name: webhook.delivery.dlq.v1
events.description: Delivery moved to DLQ after retry exhaustion.

events.name: webhook.delivery.replayed.v1
events.description: DLQ delivery re-queued by an operator (tenant-admin or projexcloud-admin).

models.description: URL + tenant + signing_key_ref + active flag. Vault holds the secret material.
(endpoint_id, event_type) join; an endpoint can subscribe to many event types.
One row per event-fanout-target. Carries current status (pending / sent / dlq / replayed) + final http_status.
Append-only attempt log per delivery: attempt_no, http_status, response_body_truncated, attempted_at.

hooks.name: registerEndpoint
hooks.description: Service entry — accepts URL + tenant + signing-key vault ref. Refuses non-HTTPS URLs in production.

hooks.name: subscribe
hooks.description: Wire an endpoint to event types. Idempotent on the (endpoint_id, event_type) pair.

hooks.name: publish
hooks.description: Fan an event out to every subscribed endpoint. Most callers don't hit this directly; sdk-audit's emitEvent pipes here when configured.

hooks.name: startDeliveryWorker
hooks.description: Background worker that polls delivery for pending rows, signs with HMAC, POSTs, advances state. Safe to leave running in dev.

scenarios.title: Customer wires their endpoint via tenant-admin
scenarios.when_to_use: Tenant admin sets up an outbound webhook so their downstream system gets notified on platform events.
scenarios.expected_outcome: Endpoint row created. Emits webhook.endpoint.registered.v1. Vault-issued signing key shown to the customer exactly once at the tenant-admin Webhooks page.

scenarios.title: Subscribe the endpoint to specific event types
scenarios.when_to_use: After registering, pick which event types fan out. Start narrow — easier to add than remove.
scenarios.expected_outcome: Two subscription rows added. Future publish() calls for either event type queue a delivery per subscribed endpoint.

scenarios.title: Worker delivers an event with HMAC signature
scenarios.when_to_use: Production background path. Worker pulls pending delivery rows, signs the payload, POSTs to the endpoint URL.
scenarios.expected_outcome: On 2xx: delivery.status='sent'. On 5xx/timeout/connect-error: exponential backoff (default 5 attempts over ~30 min). On exhaustion: delivery moves to DLQ + emits webhook.delivery.dlq.v1.

scenarios.title: Operator replays a DLQ delivery after the customer fixes their endpoint
scenarios.when_to_use: Customer admin tells us their endpoint had a config error; they've fixed it; replay everything since the failure window.
scenarios.expected_outcome: Delivery rewound to pending with attempt_no=1; worker picks it up on next tick. Emits webhook.delivery.replayed.v1 to the audit chain for compliance.

scenarios.title: Rotate the endpoint's signing key with a grace window
scenarios.when_to_use: Quarterly rotation, or after a suspected key leak. Old key valid for a 60-second overlap so the customer can swap config without dropped deliveries.
scenarios.expected_outcome: Customer can swap config any time within the 60s window with zero dropped events. Vault enforces the grace + shred timing; this SDK just records the rotation against the endpoint.

compliance_posture.notes: HTTPS-only in production (HTTP allowed only in dev mode). HMAC-SHA256 signature + timestamp prevents replay attacks beyond the 5-minute window. Signing-key secret material lives only in sdk-vault; webhook DB only ever holds the vault ref. DLQ retention default 30 days; replay-after-shred is impossible.

pricing_skus.unit_description: per active endpoint per month (free up to plan ceiling)
